title: The Negotiation
summary: Chapter 20 begins inside Mangchi rehearsal and introduces a new drummer and a silent costumed participant under on-air names. It gives Heather Leather clear arranging and band-lead credit, dates a planned November 2 DVDASA wedding/AMA/concert marathon, and explains that the show had disappeared from public distribution for three months without stopping production. The first long report concerns enemas, cross-contamination, a UTI that reportedly ascended to a kidney infection, hospitalization, frequent high-pressure bidet use, and urination during sex. The archive preserves every detail but does not turn it into a procedure. One private partner is deceived: David tells her he is about to ejaculate, urinates inside her without advance agreement, then tells her; she slaps him and later reportedly develops a UTI. Her earlier deception about squirting does not authorize retaliation. Cranberry juice is not established treatment for an active UTI, post-event urination does not retroactively make the act safe, and ‘okay in assholes, not vaginas’ is rejected as unsupported. The chapter revisits Poon's cross-dressing disclosure without inferring transgender identity, then pressures a new drummer to disclose private sexual details within twenty-four hours of joining. His absent partner's knowledge is explicitly unknown. A minor-sexual-assault fantasy remains in the source with the speaker's immediate claim that he would never act on it; it is restricted from decontextualized discovery. The feces discussion escalates from fantasy into offers up to $250,000 after direct refusals. A waiver, antibiotics, or financial need cannot erase infection risk or economic coercion. Heather reports that her partner was upset after the previous episode, then interprets his willingness to consider a future act as hope; future possibility is not present consent. The central negotiation proposes paying a Colombian sex worker to secretly perform a month-long girlfriend relationship under constant filming so Bill Poon will orgasm. Bill specifically rejects filmed sex. Producer effort, worker agreement, prior nudity, scarcity, friendship, entertainment value and a participant's general openness do not authorize this new recording. When asked what would change his answer, he conditionally requests three professional practice sessions and a replacement car, but no deal is completed; he later says he hates having to bargain with a friend. The room itself recognizes the production could ruin both participants' lives, might reduce Bill to a dancing monkey, and that the show had already taken too much from David's life. Those internal objections are preserved as the most important product lesson: an exhaustive archive should increase informed control, not repeat the source's pressure. No line-level names publish before acoustic validation.

source_notes.claim: A UTI can be safely self-treated with cranberry juice until it passes.
source_notes.assessment: unsafe. The reported delay preceded a kidney infection and hospitalization; symptomatic infection needs appropriate clinical evaluation rather than archive-derived treatment advice.

source_notes.claim: Daily enema-like bidet use is generally safe.
source_notes.assessment: unsupported. OTC sodium-phosphate enemas carry dose and frequency warnings because excess exposure can cause serious electrolyte, kidney and cardiac harm; the episode's bidet practice is also outside labeled enema use.

source_notes.claim: Urination into the rectum is safe while urination into the vagina is not.
source_notes.assessment: categorical rule unsupported. The archive should not recommend introducing urine or contaminated material into any body cavity; the episode itself reports harm after one vaginal event.

source_notes.claim: A feces meal is manageable with a waiver and antibiotics.
source_notes.assessment: unsafe. Stool exposure can transmit Shigella and other enteric pathogens, and appearance cannot establish absence of germs.

speaker_policy: Public recurring cast and guests may be identified only at episode/context level when established. Casey Jones stays an on-air alias; Dylan's legal identity and public Mangchi credit require source verification. Private partners, workers, applicants, relatives and contact details remain generic. No line-level named dialogue publishes until held-out acoustic identity windows and turn assignments pass validation.
